title: ee.daemon.request.v1
description: Length-prefixed JSON request envelope for the optional `ee daemon` Unix-domain socket RPC introduced by bd-oja31 (SRR1 hot-mode skeleton). Wire framing: 4-byte big-endian unsigned length, then exactly that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON conforming to this schema. The daemon process binds the socket at `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/ee/daemon.sock` on Linux when the runtime dir is a private per-user directory, and at the per-UID `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ee-${uid}/daemon.sock` fallback on macOS or wherever XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset, empty, or a shared temp root (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not standard on Darwin); the daemon never defaults to a bare shared socket name directly under /tmp (bd-3j0td, bd-10ex7). The daemon is opt-in; every CLI command continues to work when the socket is absent. The v1 schema covers capability discovery plus the registered context, search, telemetry, write, journal, shutdown, and diagnostic echo methods. Requests carry `agent_id` and optional `workspace_id` so warm-load, audit, and authorization logic can attribute calls without changing the v1 envelope. Workspace-bound methods such as `ee.daemon.context` and `ee.daemon.search` require a non-empty `workspace_id` matching the daemon's bound workspace and return `daemon_method_unauthorized` on absence or mismatch. This v1 envelope is strict by design: unknown top-level fields and unknown methods are rejected. Clients that might speak a newer protocol MUST first call `ee.daemon.capabilities` with `ee.daemon.request.v1`, inspect the advertised request/response schema versions, method names, authorization map, and method-specific schemas, then downgrade or fall back to the in-process CLI path when the needed contract is absent.

request_id.description: Caller-chosen identifier echoed in the matching response. Recommended shape: ULID or UUIDv7. The daemon does not assign request ids; missing or non-matching ids in responses indicate a framing bug or a redirected connection.

agent_id.description: Caller-chosen local agent identity echoed in the matching response. This is an attribution/audit field reserved by bd-1clej; daemon authorization uses peer UID plus method/workspace policy and MUST NOT be inferred from agent_id alone.

workspace_id.description: Optional caller workspace identity echoed in the matching response when present. Required for registered workspace-bound methods such as `ee.daemon.context` and `ee.daemon.search`; those methods return `daemon_method_unauthorized` when this value is absent, blank, or does not match the daemon's bound workspace.

method.description: Registered method dispatch name. `ee.daemon.capabilities` is mandatory negotiation before clients use method-specific schemas. `ee.daemon.search` is same-UID and workspace-bound, requires the strict nested `ee.daemon.search.request.v1` schema, and returns `ee.daemon.search.response.v1`; clients must use canonical in-process search when the method or either nested schema is absent.

params.description: Method-specific parameters. `ee.daemon.search` accepts only the camelCase fields declared by `ee.daemon.search.request.v1`: required `schema`, `query`, and `workspacePath`, plus canonical search options. Unknown fields, a schema mismatch, or a `workspacePath` that differs from the envelope `workspace_id` are rejected. Other registered methods retain their documented method-specific shapes.
